account: On 25 April 2024 the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration closed an engineering analysis that found that Autopilot's driver engagement system was weak for the system's permissive operation. ABC 7's WWSB reported on 24 April 2026 that a Tesla had stopped in the middle lane of Interstate 75 near Sarasota. Florida Highway Patrol officers found 37-year-old Kimberly Brown asleep behind the wheel at about 2 a.m. The station quotes Trooper Kenn Watson and reports that she was arrested for driving under the influence. It reports that the car came to a halt in the middle lane when Brown stopped responding to the vehicle's alerts. The report says that she had expected Autopilot to take her home. Edmunds analyst Alistair Weaver explains the general driver-attention warning and stopping mechanism. The report does not include vehicle logs that establish the precise sequence in this car. Gray News, citing state police, reported that troopers found Brown at about 2 a.m. on Friday, 24 April 2026. It reported that the troopers credited the car's eye detection with bringing it to a halt. Ouest-France reported on 3 May 2026 that her blood alcohol level was more than twice the legal limit.

ai_role.statement: Florida Highway Patrol troopers attribute the stop to the car's eye detection. WWSB reports that the car halted in the middle lane when the driver stopped responding to its alerts. The driver's decision to rely on Autopilot while drunk created the danger. No vehicle data were published to confirm the sequence.

A stop-in-lane or shoulder-stop fallback when warnings go unanswered

purpose: Autopilot's driver-attention monitoring is built to warn an inattentive driver. It brings the car to a stop if the driver does not respond. It is not designed to drive an impaired person home.

ratings.reason: The car stopped with its intoxicated driver asleep and without a crash. No vehicle data or other source establishes what harm the stop averted, so the extent of the benefit cannot be established.
The car came to rest in the middle lane of I-75, and no source documents a collision with other road users that the stop prevented.

summary: Troopers said that the eye detection feature of a Tesla on Autopilot halted the car on I-75 after its intoxicated driver fell asleep; no vehicle data confirm the sequence.
system: Tesla Autopilot, according to the reported account; the vehicle model and active configuration are unverified.
title: A Tesla on Autopilot stops in the middle lane of I-75 with its drunk driver asleep; police arrest her for driving under the influence
unrated_because: The sources report that the car stopped while its drunk driver slept and that no one was hurt, and they do not establish what harm the stop averted for her or for other road users.
